reviews.review: For me this is new game experience that you can enjoy the story via monitor. The story line push me to keep playing to find out more what will happen next and what is the next puzzle to solve. The puzzles level for me is moderate to slightly high but its worth solving each one of them and Its feel great though when beat some puzzles. They created unique puzzles that I can cannot imagine how they came up with these.
this game is only 3 hours long

Pretty decent conspiracy thriller with a good twist to the story. Mostly deals with identity and the purpose of your job at the FDI. Has a cliffhanger ending which burns the experience a bit. The only time I struggled with the game is with the bomb defusal which is the most frustrating to do in the game, other than that I loved how the desktop plays a huge role in uncovering clues. You become either a loyal agent or an espionage spy which it does pretty well to keep the player engaged.

Price wise it's a bit on the expensive side for only 3-4 hours of gameplay so I would wait for a sale overall. This is the closest to something X-files, Bones or Mindhunter just as tv show examples would've done in a videogame format in the perspective of a techie. Hopefully if the sequel is released it can expand on the underdeveloped tools like the sample analysis for example, have multiple endings and remove the time limited puzzles. The opportunity to do multiple cases (subplots which would either help your detective or not) instead of following the main story would be amazing potential as well if that's possible too.
Excellent, I wish it was longer!

Very fun game! I really like the tense atmosphere and overarching narrative. While I wish the game was 2-3x longer, I really enjoyed my play through and look forward to future projects from this studio.
A Great game with a good plot and the in game photo is a nice touch seeing my face in a game made my day hope for more (a DLC or sequel)
A great narrative game! And I also liked searching answers for the agents on the computer.

This is easily one of the best concepts for a game that I've ever seen. 
It scratched an itch that no other game has, and the story and gameplay were absolutely amazing. 
HOWEVER, I wish it was longer. The entire game was just one crime, and my actions had almost no impact on what actually happened. If my actions mattered a little more, and there were more crimes to solve, this game would be absolutely perfect.

If you love crime tv shows and alway felt like you could work in dispatch..this is the game for you!! I played it from top to bottom in once sitting. It kept me on the edge of my seat the the whole time and had some pretty shocking plot twists. Highly recommend!

Hi, I'm arko, I can give a little bit of backstory;

When I was a younger kid, I always loved the idea of discovering a crime, investigating, solving cases, it just scratched an itch and ideas I had for my brain.

Almost a decade later and I still enjoy such, I love ARG's, and such, and whenever I find one, I try my absolute HARDEST to solve.

I started off with the Kaigan Games, Games, Sara is Missing, popularized in the late 2010's, you take perspective as a person who has found Sara's phone, and tries to investigate by asking her friends, family, and debunk cultist relations. Later on, I moved onto the SIMULACRA series, though not totally investigative games, they follow a similar principle, I loved SIMULACRA 1, and replayed it 4 times. It just satisfied me a way other games have not.

I found out about this game way before release, I became excited to purchase it, though I did not buy it day one, I bought it extremely early. This game, scratched an itch no other games I listed prior and ARG's that I didn't even know existed. 

The way the game functions, the calls, everything that's in this game, is great. I love the operating system, and I think this is by far one of the best interpretations of a call center in the 80's-2000's. Everything from the keyboard sounds, the ambiance behind you, the mouse clicking, the computer effect, is so immersive, and I believe this is one of the most immersive games, I have ever played.

-----------------------------------------------------

My opinions on the story, there will be spoilers.

You start off the game with a cutscene, you are being questioned by someone in an absurdly bright white room, there's nothing there but white. At first, you will think this cutscene means nothing, and is useless, but at the end, it will totally blow your mind, I won't say it here, as I want YOU to experience the thrill and twists this game has to offer. 

The immersive and keep you on your toes gameplay, especially with the bomb you have to deal with to make sure an Agent doesn't die, the back and forth with the notepad, manual, call, commands, is extremely thrilling, and keeps you nervous and anxious, as one wrong move, will kill the person you are trying to save.

The use of a system that has a database, is great, scanning cars, people, places, and objects to help solve cases is amazing, and I believe it is the best yet.

-------------------------------------

Overall review

Gameplay: 6.5/10
Story: 11/10
Graphics: 5/10
Cinematics: 5.5/10
Sound Design: 10/10
Soundtrack: 10/10


This game has practically confirmed others are planned, due to the end credits and the last thing you do, so I really expect and hope for another installment.

Great game, maybe too short, but still great. I need second part. The game has many interesting aspects that show its potential. I hope it will be implemented in the second part. [spoiler] Moments like when I checked the director's marital status after talking about his wife, or the conversation with the secretary where she checks me with the name of the guy from the IT department [/spoiler], these are very cool suspenseful moments. More non-linearity, deeper investigation and gameplay variations are what this game needs. But the first impression is very satisfactory.

The aesthetic is amazing and if you're a spy story or retro tech nerd you'll absolutely love it. 

However, there are some grating issues with the story. [spoiler]Even if you do everything right you're still fucked in the end, and in a very unlikely way that is hard to suspend disbelief for. [/spoiler] I mean, how the hell does  [spoiler]the building security be so incompetent as to let a man escape, murder THE DIRECTOR, murder a senior supervisor,  and murder an operator?[/spoiler] I mean, that's just absurd! I get they're alluding to it being because of a conspiracy  [spoiler] where Security allowed it to happen[/spoiler] but it's just too over the top. And then the fact that [spoiler]absolutely everyone remotely involved with the situation dies[/spoiler] is leaning so hard into the tropes of the genre that it's about to knock them over.

The game itself is the opposite of life fuel because of [spoiler]the path the story inevitably follows with no opportunity for the player to avert it[/spoiler] but at the same time can be considered a kind of high art for that same reason. The Operator perfectly captures the sense of [spoiler]hopelessness[/spoiler] a person would feel when [spoiler]going up against "THEM" from all your favorite Alex Jones conspiracies.[/spoiler]

The [spoiler]MKULTRA[/spoiler] program holds a special place in my heart, and the nods to it in this game were like reading through the project files. 

Speaking of reading through the project files, a list of all [spoiler]149 currently [/spoiler] known sub-projects has somehow made its way onto [spoiler]The Internet Archive[/spoiler] as a PDF file named  [spoiler]"MKULTRA Briefing Book List Of Subprojects With Brief Descriptions January 1976"[/spoiler]

This review has been redacted by [spoiler]Hiram Abiff[/spoiler] on [spoiler]8/4/2024[/spoiler]

It's... fine. The story, the big twist, the whole shebang, you can make a pretty good guess at early in the story. As others have pointed out, you are given lots of tools that you use only once, and the description of "solve crimes" isn't correct, since you only do one case really and I wouldn't say you truly solve it. Also, some may find the end of the game unsatisfying. I was one of those people. The story feels quite linear, with only 1 real point where it didn't feel like the game was railroading you into the next part of the story.  

But that's not say that the game doesn't have merit. It just feels like an expensive game demo that leaves you wishing that there was a full game for you to play. If you are looking for something like Papers Please, you aren't going to find it here.

Probably one of the best short story games I have ever played. The play through was amazing and the feel of the game almost like it was really a FDI terminal. I would play this a few times over again to see what I missed. Would highly recommend this game for a fun little story. I hope they release another game that follows the same theme and style would definitely play that.

One of the reasons I play games now for as long as I have is for its story and I liked this game's premise starting out because it had a lot of potential, However the one thing I particularly love about a video game's story over a book or TV show is the immersion and replay value, however the story was too short and linear for that. It should've started with the first few cases being separate from the main case to build onto the story and flesh out more connection with the characters. That way at least the ending would've had more of an impact than a cliffhanger that doesn't really support a sequel to be had whether the developer wants to make one or not.

This was a great little game, really captures the 90's X-Files vibes. You play as Tanner, who is part of a new class of agent called an operator. Agents call into to you and get you to do analysis. Who is the mysterious hacker? What has caused all these deaths? Who is the unknown man?

Would highly recommend if you are into Orwell or other games of this type.

Extremely disappointed to see they used AI for some of the art (hire artists instead of stealing from them, please), but it looks to have been very limited so I'll still give them a recommended. Hopefully their next game won't have any of that.

It's a good game, and I enjoyed it. It's clear it was made with love, but unfortunately, it's very linear for me. The game practically holds your hand through the story, leaving you no room to make your own choices. You're forced to do things you might not want to do. For example, at the beginning, I tried to resist and wanted to shout, "Catch Hal!" I even tried making unauthorized ip-calls to my superiors to report Hal via the terminal, but the game didn't allow such actions. This is a big downside for me. I want to make my own decisions rather than choosing from a set of predetermined responses. The game doesn't even offer the illusion of choice.

I won't lie – I had to look up a walkthrough on Google to solve the bomb puzzle, and I hate puzzles. Why?
All puzzles have only one solution, and that doesn't work for me.

I really enjoyed the game overall but for a game with no replyability at all - I have mixed feelings about the price. I made peace with it purely because the team did seem to invest in the voice actors and some limited filming which can be costly and it does enrich the game.

The story is good if a tad predictable, but design is good and the game does reward staying observant in ways you may not expect.

There are cases though where I noticed things and the game treated me as if I hadn't - suggesting moments where the Devs perhaps thought they were being cleverer than they were.

I finished it in 2hr 48mins and did enjoy it, the price is acceptable for the quality I feel but the game deserves and desperately needs a bigger sequel with more cases and replyability and perhaps a small discount for those of us who bought the first proof of concept game.

If you can spare the money, it's worthwhile evenings entertainment.

The game is a missed opportunity, a project that could have been one of my favorite games.

The game starts off very slow, gets quite exciting in the middle, and ends in the worst possible way.

It feels like being on a roller coaster ride where you're stuck on a track and can't explore or solve mysteries freely. The puzzles are either simple or downright pathetic. Anyone who enjoys mysteries and has read a couple of detective novels could finish the game in under 3 hours. There's a part in the game that's quite exciting and was my favorite, but it ends quickly, leaving a bittersweet feeling.

If this game had followed in the footsteps of similar games like Hacknet, it could have been a masterpiece in the genre. Instead, it turned into an interactive movie, like a typical Sony game.

I'd recommend it if you find it for under 5 euros, as it only offers about 4 hours of gameplay at most.

This game is well worth it for the price! The puzzles are challenging but logical (The best place for puzzle difficulty to sit). It often reminds me of document management games like Papers Please and those who've played the game will know a certain segment's similarities to Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. My only major complaint is that the game feels short for what it is. Even if it isn't plot related, the gameplay of diving through files to find the connections is so addictive I would've happily enjoyed several more hours of it, but on the other hand I feel like if my main complaint is that your game didn't have enough filler, you've definitely won my approval.

Pick it up while it's on sale or pay full price and support the devs.

Oh and to the devs: MAKE A SEQUEL! PLEASE! Some DLC at LEAST!

I never reviewed a game on Steam before but I have to say THIS GAME IS AMAZING. I always struggle to stick to a game, no matter how short is is. This game has made be glued to my screen till the end.

I am the fan of the stories in games, and "The Operator" has just reached the top with this engaging storyline. What made it so cool is that the plot was very catchy, so it kept me playing. I could only wish for more depth in some storylines, making them way more complicated and detailed. Just a few more levels of detail in the story would make the experience even more puzzling and immersive. 

The game needs the possibility of side tasks that would help to. It would provide depth to the experience and variety of mundaneness, because otherwise, having some really mundane cases that are not related to the main story might make it feel more real and alive. The game mechanics were great! Simple and comprehensible, suitable for many players. My only complaint is that the game felt a bit too short.

Something like statistics about what choices I made would be great; for instance, what percentage of the other players made the same decisions. That would be a great addition concerning interactive replay. The user interface in the game, especially the terminal interface, was so awkward in the context of the end of the 1990s since it felt very modern. A more period-appropriate design would add to the overall sense of immersion and give a more authentic feeling to the game. All in all, "The Operator" is quite a compelling game with a good story and intuitive mechanics.
